title: Greece Travel Guide 2026: Athens, Santorini & Islands
description: Greece itineraries covering the Acropolis, Santorini sunsets and island hopping, with Greek food, a EUR budget and Schengen visa tips for Indians.

sections.title: Why Visit Greece?
sections.html:
Greece is a land of ancient history, stunning natural beauty, and island paradise. From the Acropolis overlooking Athens to Santorini's legendary blue-domed sunset views, from ancient ruins of Delphi to island-hopping adventures, Greece captivates with myths, history, and Mediterranean charm. Perfect for history buffs, beach lovers, culture seekers, and romantics.

Explore ancient temples, swim in crystal-clear turquoise seas, enjoy legendary Greek hospitality, taste Mediterranean cuisine, and experience timeless island life. Greece is unforgettable.

sections.title: 3-Day Greece Itinerary
sections.html: A 3-day plan with morning, afternoon and evening ideas and an approximate daily cost per person. Use it as a starting point and adjust to your pace.

days.title: Athens: Acropolis & Ancient Ruins
periods: Arrive at Athens airport. Metro to hotel (EUR 10). Visit Acropolis (EUR 20). See Parthenon, Erechtheion - ancient temples. Grab Greek coffee and loukoumades (fried pastry, EUR 4-6).
Explore Acropolis Museum (EUR 9). Walk historic Plaka neighborhood - charming streets, tavernas (free). Visit Temple of Olympian Zeus (EUR 6). Browse local shops and galleries.
Traditional Greek dinner at taverna (EUR 15-25) - moussaka, souvlaki, Greek salad. Greek wine (EUR 4-8 per glass). Evening walk through Syntagma Square. Sunset from Areopagus Hill (free).

days.title: Delphi Day Trip: Ancient Oracle
periods: Coach/rental car to Delphi (EUR 20-40 round trip, 2 hours). Visit Delphi Archaeological Site (EUR 12) - ancient sanctuary of Apollo. Dramatic clifftop setting. Museum included (EUR 6 separate). Breakfast en route (EUR 6-10).
Walk Theater of Delphi ruins (included). Visit Delphi Museum to see treasures. Explore nearby town of Delphi (free wandering). Lunch at local taverna (EUR 12-18).
Return to Athens. Dinner (EUR 15-25). Rest from travel day or explore Psyrri district for nightlife.

days.title: Santorini: Sunset & Island Life
periods: Ferry Athens to Santorini (EUR 40-60, 7 hours or fly EUR 50-80, 1 hour). Arrive, check into Oia or Fira. Relax at volcanic black sand beach (free). Grab Greek yogurt with honey (EUR 4-6).

Explore Fira town - whitewashed buildings, blue domes (free wandering). Cable car down to beach (EUR 4) or walk volcanic steps (free). Swimming in Aegean Sea (free). Wine tasting at winery (EUR 15-25).
Watch famous Santorini sunset from Oia (free, arrive early). Dinner overlooking caldera (EUR 20-40). Feta saganaki, fresh fish, Santorini wine. Late-night walk through village squares.

sections.title: Greece Food Guide
sections.html:
Greek cuisine is fresh, healthy, and celebrated worldwide. Mediterranean ingredients - olive oil, feta, olives, fresh vegetables - form the foundation. Food is social, meant for sharing.

Must-Try Dishes

  • Moussaka – Eggplant, meat, béchamel layered bake. Cost: EUR 10-15
  • Souvlaki – Grilled meat on skewers. Cost: EUR 6-12
  • Horiatiki Salad – Greek salad with feta and olives. Cost: EUR 8-12
  • Saganaki – Fried cheese. Cost: EUR 6-9
  • Spanakopita – Spinach and feta pie. Cost: EUR 4-8
  • Gyros – Rotisserie meat wrap. Cost: EUR 3-6
  • Loukoumades – Honey puffs dessert. Cost: EUR 4-6
  • Baklava – Nut and honey pastry. Cost: EUR 3-5

Best Food Spots

  • Tavernas – Traditional family dining, communal atmosphere
  • Fish Restaurants – Fresh Mediterranean seafood
  • Street Food – Gyros, souvlaki, affordable quick bites
  • Local Markets – Fresh produce, cheeses, olives

sections.title: Best Time to Visit Greece
sections.html:
Best overall: May-June and September-October (sunny, warm 22-28°C, fewer crowds than summer)

Summer swimming: July-August (hot 28-35°C, crowded, expensive, perfect for islands)

Avoid: July-August peak (extremely crowded, very hot, highest prices)

Budget tip: November-March (mild 10-16°C, rainy, lowest prices and fewer tourists)

sections.title: Getting Around Greece
sections.html:
Metro & Buses

Athens metro well-developed. Single ticket: EUR 1.40. Day pass: EUR 4.50. Island buses are affordable (EUR 1-3 per ride).

Ferries

Extensive ferry network. Athens to Santorini: EUR 40-80. Many ferry companies - book ahead in peak season to save 20-30%.

Taxis & Ride-share

Taxis metered in cities. Grab available in Athens. Within cities: EUR 5-12 typical fare.

Organized Tours

Island hopping tours: EUR 50-80. Walking tours: EUR 15-25. Sunset boat cruises: EUR 30-50.

sections.title: Travel Essentials
sections.html:
Visa & Entry

Visa for Indians: a Schengen short-stay visa is required. Apply through the Greece visa centre in India (VFS Global or the appointed provider) if Greece is your main destination, up to 6 months and at least 15 days before you travel. The fee is €90 for adults, processing usually takes about 15 days (longer in summer), and you need travel insurance with at least €30,000 medical cover. The visa allows up to 90 days in any 180-day period across the Schengen area. Rules as of October 2026; always check the official website before you apply.

Currency & Money

Euro (EUR). Exchange rate: 1 EUR ≈ 1.10 USD. ATMs widely available. Tipping optional (5-10% appreciated).

Budget Breakdown (per day, budget traveler)

  • Accommodation: EUR 20-40 (hostels, budget hotels)
  • Food: EUR 15-30 (tavernas, street food)
  • Transport: EUR 3-8 (buses, metro)
  • Activities: EUR 15-35 (museums, attractions)
  • Total: EUR 55-115/day (~$60-127 USD)

Important Notes

  • Greek siesta culture - many shops close 2-5pm.
  • Dinner typically 8-11pm. Don't expect restaurants full before 9pm.
  • Islands can be windy - pack light layers.
  • Ferry schedules change seasonally - check in advance.
  • Greek hospitality warm and welcoming - locals appreciate effort to speak Greek.
